title: ReachReason
description: Why a tier refused to serve an object under a root (interfaces spec §A.3). To a requester outside reach, a missing object and a private one get the same refusal, naming the requester's missing standing and not the object (spec §12.3 rule 2). `not-under-root` is said only for a path proved absent in a held node; `no-record` means the tier holds no reach record for the root and refused rather than fetching one; `index-warming` means the serving daemon has not completed its first artifact-index rebuild, so absence is not established yet; there is no admit-on-error path. Source of truth: this schema; Rust mirror `eprfs_core::ReachReason` (eprfs-core/src/reach.rs, kebab-case serde), pinned in eprfs-core's schema_contract test. Not named in §2.G's enum list; added because objects/item-absence's `refused.refusal.reason` needs a referenced vocabulary (CONVENTIONS rule 7). Carries neither `_dna` nor `_codegen`: it is a field vocabulary for the placement wire schemas, generated only as a TypeScript union where those schemas inline it, and adds no constant to schema-enums.ts.
